name: Moral Machine
tagline: A platform for exploring ethical dilemmas in autonomous vehicle decision-making through crowdsourced data collection
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
known_funders: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
dependency_risks: Institutional dependency on MIT Media Lab

news_articles.headline: Moral Machine: A Global Study of Ethical Preferences in Autonomous Vehicles

policy_outcomes: Informed discussions on autonomous vehicle ethics in academic and policy circles
Referenced in AI ethics frameworks and guidelines
outcome_methodology: Crowdsourced preference aggregation study with global participation
published_performance_metrics: 10+ million responses from 233 countries and territories
jurisdictional_scope: Global with varying participation rates by region
failure_modes: Ethical dilemmas presented may not reflect real-world autonomous vehicle scenarios
curation_criteria: Ethical dilemmas presented in standardized format with visual representations (skull for death, medical cross for injury, question mark for uncertain outcomes); responses aggregated by demographic and geographic variables
contributor_governance: Open participation model; users can judge scenarios, design custom scenarios, and browse/discuss community-created content; no formal contributor governance structure documented
disparity_tracking: Tracked by country, age, gender, and education level in published analyses
controversies: Criticism that the platform oversimplifies complex ethical decision-making in autonomous vehicles
Concerns about cultural bias in ethical preference aggregation
ai_involvement: Core to project design - studying AI ethical decision-making
political_relevance_summary: Moral Machine addresses the civic problem of making civic data accessible and actionable. It has documented policy impact.

movement_building_utility.notes: Serves as an information resource: A platform for exploring ethical dilemmas in autonomous vehicle decision-making through crowdsourced data collection.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase enables replication. already deployed internationally across multiple jurisdictions.
